intro: You play a 58-year-old logistics manager who is suddenly job-hunting after 28 years. The hard part is not what he can do but what employers assume about his age. His experience and his network are real assets.

tunnel.why: Online filters and silent rejections: you never learn why your application vanished.

quiet.why: 28 years of judgement: Jonas reads a situation and a plan calmly and quickly.

bridge.why: Old colleagues and mentors carry him: Mira's tip and Aylin's help matter more than any form.

advantage.title: Seen it before
advantage.text: After decades in logistics Jonas has seen many problems before and can rule out unlikely answers. Remove one wrong answer before you answer.

life.title: Monday morning (fictional)
life.text: Jonas is an invented character. He is 58, a logistics manager with 28 years in one company, well liked and reliable. Then his company is taken over.

life.title: Redundancy
life.text: Jonas is told his position is being cut as part of a restructuring. Younger, cheaper staff stay. He has done nothing wrong.

life.title: The first search
life.text: He sends dozens of applications. Many get no reply. At interviews he is asked how he feels about reporting to someone younger.

life.title: "Overqualified"
life.text: Employers assume older workers cost more, adapt less or leave sooner. Jonas has the skills, but the stereotype reaches the desk before he does.

life.title: A word for it
life.text: What Jonas meets has a name, which the WHO uses in its global report.

q.q: What is prejudice or discrimination based on age called?
q.x: Ageism means stereotypes and unfair treatment because of age. The WHO's 2021 global report treats it as a widespread problem.

life.title: Online forms and tests
life.text: Long web forms and tests are new to Jonas. Without help he feels lost, and there is no box where 28 years of experience can show.

life.title: A tip from Mira
life.text: A former colleague, Mira, hears of an opening in a smaller firm and passes it on. Personal networks often count more than the formal process.

life.title: The oldest in class
life.text: Jonas retrains for a new field. Some classmates are friendly. Others assume he will not keep up. Having to prove himself again wears him down.

life.title: Swapping skills with Aylin
life.text: A young classmate, Aylin, shows him new software. He shows her how to lead a team. Both of them leave the course better off.

life.title: Mixed-age teams
life.text: Jonas's next team has people from many age groups.

q.q: What does research usually say about teams of mixed ages?
a: They work well, since each age group brings different strengths
q.x: Studies suggest age-diverse teams do well, because experience and fresh ideas complement each other.

life.title: A new role
life.text: A company hires Jonas as an operations coordinator. His new manager says his experience is exactly what the team has been missing.

life.title: Not too old
life.text: Jonas now trains younger colleagues. He says: "Nobody warned me that you can be treated as too old long before you feel old." He backs hiring that looks at skills, not birth years.
